public_rationale: The records establish substantial construction obstacles, but not the claimed industry-wide majority of incomplete projects. Sightline identifies a large unstarted pipeline; JLL reports widespread delays in the preceding year. Neither measures full completion among projects due in the target quarter. CBRE also documents substantial occupied capacity, which cautions against treating delays as an absence of delivery. The available evidence cannot fairly establish or reject the complete claim.
limitations: The period, project population, and meaning of full completion require interpretation.
The strongest broad delay and occupancy figures describe 2025, so they are context only.
A future delivery date cannot be treated as a missed deadline.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The stalled Nebius Vineland project reflects an industry-wide problem: data centers are hard to build and mostly are not being fully built.

statement.excerpt: This is bad, and indicative of a larger problem in the industry — that it’s really difficult to build data centers, and for the most part, they’re not being fully built!
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: a larger problem in the industry
really difficult to build data centers
for the most part, they’re not being fully built
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that construction difficulties are widespread and most new data-center projects are failing to reach their intended full operational build-out.
I interpret 'for the most part' as more than half of projects by count. The speaker does not specify a geography, project cohort, or capacity-weighted measure.
For this ongoing observation, I use January–March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter that public evidence could describe before the May 12 post.
Full completion means delivery of the project's announced operational scope. Completing one building does not establish completion of a larger campus.
To distinguish construction failure from normal construction in progress, the completion test requires original delivery schedules. Future phases that were not yet due do not establish failure.
criteria.support_condition: Representative project-level records for the target period show widespread construction obstacles and more than half of projects due for full delivery remaining incomplete, stalled, or abandoned.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that at least half of projects due for full delivery reached their intended operational scope, contradicting the majority assertion. Evidence that construction obstacles were uncommon would separately contradict the difficulty assertion.
